In the mathematical field of [[Riemannian geometry]], the '''Reilly formula''' is an important [[Identity (mathematics)|identity]], discovered by Robert Reilly in 1977.<ref>{{harvnb|Reilly|1977}}</ref> It says that, given a smooth [[Riemannian manifold|Riemannian]] [[manifold with boundary|manifold-with-boundary]] {{math|(''M'', ''g'')}} and a [[smooth function]] {{mvar|u}} on {{mvar|M}}, one has
:<math>\int_{\partial M}\left(H\Big(\frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}\Big)^2+2\frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}\Delta^{\partial M}u+h\big(\nabla^{\partial M}u,\nabla^{\partial M}u\big)\right)=\int_M \Big((\Delta u)^2-|\nabla\nabla u|^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla u,\nabla u)\Big),</math>
in which {{mvar|h}} is the [[second fundamental form]] of the boundary of {{mvar|M}}, {{mvar|H}} is its [[mean curvature]], and {{math|ν}} is its unit normal vector.<ref>Chow, Lu, and Ni, section A.5</ref><ref>Colding and Minicozzi, section 7.3</ref> This is often used in combination with the observation
:<math>|\nabla\nabla u|^2=\frac{1}{n}(\Delta u)^2+\Big|\nabla\nabla u-\frac{1}{n}(\Delta u)g\Big|^2\geq\frac{1}{n}(\Delta u)^2,</math>
with the consequence that
:<math>\int_{\partial M}\left(H\Big(\frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}\Big)^2+2\frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}\Delta^{\partial M}u+h\big(\nabla^{\partial M}u,\nabla^{\partial M}u\big)\right)\leq\int_M \Big(\frac{n-1}{n}(\Delta u)^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla u,\nabla u)\Big).</math>
This is particularly useful since one can now make use of the solvability of the Dirichlet problem for the Laplacian to make useful choices for {{mvar|u}}.<ref>Li, section 8</ref><ref>Schoen and Yau, section III.8</ref> Applications include eigenvalue estimates in [[spectral geometry]] and the study of submanifolds of [[Constant-mean-curvature surface|constant mean curvature]].
